_README: Every test in kind auth's contract suite (tests/test-data-auth.js) that the ROW judge is
expected to disagree with, and why. Regenerate the NAMES with:
but never regenerate the REASONS mechanically — an entry without a reason someone wrote is
the whole thing this fixture exists to prevent.
Categories: default | field | create | harness | cosmetic | OPEN
SCOPE OF THIS CHECK: test-data-auth.js's fixtures declare NO authVocabulary, so every
run here exercises the LEGACY SHIM path (legacyVerbs.js). A migrated app does not use it —
all 81 pattern rows on rowauth-test declare, and a declared vocabulary wins over the shim.
The declared path is covered in tests/test-row-auth-writes.js, 'a DECLARED vocabulary'.

2026-11-03: six attribute-clause cases were added to test-data-auth.js (page section_groups / dataSources, site tenants / dms_envs, the tenant and dmsenv kinds, source views-only) when kind auth's hand-written switch was replaced by the authRules.js + authJudge.js interpreter — they pin clauses nothing had pinned before, verified identical on BOTH judges before the switch went. All six disagree with row auth: one for the known `field` reason, five because site-level grants live on a sibling pattern row. Both were already understood; they had simply never been measured.

2026-11-03 (unified-auth-api.md Phase 1): the `field` reason and all four of its entries are GONE. Which attribute needs which verb is declared in the format that owns the attribute (`permissionDomain` entries carry `fields`), read by both implementations through `verbsForFields`. Row auth asks for the named verb rather than what it implies — `publish-page` and `edit-page` imply the same structural verbs, so asking for implications let any page editor publish, which is what that reason recorded. `noChange` resolved with it: the any-of group for an empty change set is derived from the claims instead of listed.

2026-11-03 (unified-auth-api.md Phase 4): site-level grants now live on the `:site` ROW, which parentage can reach, instead of only on the admin pattern row beside it. Six more entries resolved with that plus Phase 1's scoped field maps — including the OPEN `scope collapse` widening, where a FLAT `edit-page` grant on a pattern row also conferred editing the pattern row itself: the field map is per scope now, so `edit-page` claims fields only under `descendants`.

2026-11-03 (unified-auth-api.md): the four entries left under `sibling-grants` were re-pinned — that reason described none of them any more. Phase 4 put site grants on the site row, which resolved the sibling case itself; what remained were three different causes wearing its label: `cross-owner` (a field judged against another row's grants), `named-create` (a create asks for the structural verb) and `no-pattern-lending` (the source states nothing and the pattern no longer lends). A wrong reason is worse than no reason: it makes a live gap look settled.
cascade: U on a page: stranger 403, anon 401, editor 200
U judges the stored type, not the one the client names
_cascade_note: Not disagreements at all. test-data-auth.js's race test restores docsPage.authPermissions
AFTER its try/finally, so when its assertion fails it leaks users:{10:['edit-page']} into every
later test. These three then fail for that reason. Moving those two lines into the finally
takes the run from 26 failures to 23. Their file, their call — raised, not patched.

reasons.default: STRICT DEFAULTS, decided (hub). Kind auth: signed-in + no grants ⇒ open. Row auth: writes need a grant. Every app with unconfigured patterns loses editing on an enforce flip — the Phase D audit script is a prerequisite.
reasons.create: WHAT A CREATE IS JUDGED AGAINST. Without a claimed parent_id the type path routes docs|page and docs|component to the same pattern row, so one `create` verb cannot tell 'add a section' from 'add a page'. Accepted: a page created with its sections IS 'add a page to this pattern'.
reasons.harness: NOT A DISAGREEMENT. These drive their race by hooking controller.getPatternRows — kind auth's pattern-grant lookup. The row judge never calls it, so the concurrent edit never fires. The protection they test (expect + assertRowUnchanged) is in the ROUTE, gate-independent and unchanged.
reasons.cosmetic: Behaviour is right (allowed under log, one line written). The assertion matches '[data-auth] … missing edit-page'; the row gate writes '[row-auth] … reason=missing edit'.
reasons.cross-owner: A FIELD JUDGED AGAINST ANOTHER ROW'S GRANTS, which a vocabulary cannot express. The site row's `dms_envs` is governed by the DATASETS pattern's grants, not the site's — kind auth says so with `byKey: { dms_envs: { anyOf: [{ owner: 'datasets-grants', ... }] } }`, the one clause left in authRules.js after Phase 1 moved the rest into the formats. A `fields` claim names a verb, and a verb is held on the row being judged; there is no way to say "this field is judged somewhere else". So the site's vocabulary claims nothing for `dms_envs`, row auth falls through to a plain structural `edit`, and ROW AUTH IS LOOSER HERE — a site editor holding `manage-themes` can register a dmsEnv. Bound: one field on one row kind. Fixing it needs an owner concept in the vocabulary, which is a design decision, not an omission.
reasons.named-create: A CREATE ASKS FOR THE STRUCTURAL VERB, a named one is not consulted. Row auth judges a create as `create` on the parent's chain; kind auth asks for the kind's named verb (`manage-tenants` for a tenant, `create-source`/`edit-pattern` for a dmsEnv). A holder of `manage-tenants` has `read` and `edit` and not `create`, so row auth refuses what kind auth allows — it fails closed. Phase 1 gave EDITS their named verbs through `fields`; a create has no changed fields to claim, so the same mechanism does not reach it. Fixing it means letting a kind declare which verb governs creating it, which is a vocabulary addition nobody has asked for yet.
reasons.no-pattern-lending: DECIDED, not discovered (owner, 2026-11-02). A datasets PATTERN is not a source's ancestor — a source's type is `{env}|{name}:source` and the pattern is nowhere in the path — so its grants no longer reach sources (row-auth-uda-unify-api.md Slice K). Kind auth still lends them. Here the editor's `create-view` / `update-source` sit on the ds pattern and the source itself states nothing, so the field claim fires correctly and finds no holder. The grant sweep (`scripts/sweep-source-grants.js`) is what closes this per app; on `rowauth-test` it reports zero remaining.
